text:
incident-bot: PAGED maya-oncall: suspicious log exposure detected. 3 distinct IPs fetching objects from s3://redwood-logs-staging/2026-03-18/ — pattern: X-Auth header fragments present in objects. Severity: P1. Runbook: https://wiki/redwood/incidents/s3-leak
maya-oncall: got it. jumping in. first pass: confirm scope and isolate bucket access. @eli-sre please snapshot current bucket ACLs and list recent GETs.
eli-sre: running quick queries now. sample from access logs:
```
2026-03-18T21:02:12 GET s3://redwood-logs-staging/2026-03-18/trace-7a.log 200 "-" "10.11.12.13"
2026-03-18T21:02:14 GET s3://redwood-logs-staging/2026-03-18/trace-9f.log 200 "-" "52.78.11.9"
```
Found objects with short auth snippets: `Authorization: Bearer eyJhbGci...snip...` (not full tokens present, but fragments). looks like dev tooling uploaded full traces including headers.
sanjay-platform: that bucket was recently enabled by a dev onboarding script. I see a new lifecycle policy and a public-read ACL accidentally applied on 2026-03-18T20:58 by ci-bot. locking ACL now -> `aws s3api put-bucket-acl --bucket redwood-logs-staging --acl private` :thumbsup:
lisa-security: escalate: treat as credential exposure. Immediate actions: 1) revoke any short-lived tokens that could be reconstructed; 2) rotate service account keys that wrote to that bucket; 3) wipe exposed objects and coordinate with backups. I'll start a KMS key rotate if resources used that key. also notify legal if customer data suspected. @legal-bot please queue review.
maya-oncall: quick customer impact check: early indication is internal/staging only, not production. @sanjay-platform confirm whether any prod bucket used same pipeline.
sanjay-platform: confirmed: prod buckets unaffected, different pipeline and IAM roles. staging CI service account `ci-staging-logger` had write perms. I'll rotate its access keys and block any new token issuance.
eli-sre: running a fast grep for `Authorization: Bearer` across bucket objects to enumerate leaks. found ~12 files with header fragments. tagging objects for deletion: `aws s3api delete-object --bucket redwood-logs-staging --key 2026-03-18/trace-9f.log` — will run in 2m after snapshot.
lisa-security: hold on deletion until forensic snapshot is complete. we need E2E snapshot for legal/forensics. eli, upload snapshot to secure-case-bucket (restricted) and note object versions. then mark objects for deletion.
eli-sre: copying snapshot now to `s3://secure-case-bucket/incident-1819012345/` and noting versions.
maya-oncall: action list: 
- @sanjay-platform rotate `ci-staging-logger` keys (in progress)
- @eli-sre snapshot + mark for delete (in progress)
- @lisa-security coordinate KMS rotate + revocations (assigning)
- @legal-bot prepare statement + retention hold (pending)
please react with :white_check_mark: when done.
sanjay-platform: rotated keys and revoked old tokens for `ci-staging-logger`. pushed policy to block old keys and force new creds for all staging CI agents. Command used: `rctl iam rotate --service ci-staging-logger --force` — logs show success.
lisa-security: kicked off KMS rewrap job for the key used by logger pipeline. running integrity check and will provide ETA. Also starting a quick run of token-usage lookup to see if fragments map to any active sessions.
eli-sre: snapshot complete and stored under secure-case-bucket. created deletion ticket but holding until security says go. object count: 12. accessible IPs: ["10.11.12.13","52.78.11.9","3.120.45.6"].
maya-oncall: good work. customer impact still appears none. prepare a short internal postmortem stub we can update. @lisa-security move to severity P1->P1 (confirmed) and coordinate external comms if legal requests.
lisa-security: legal-bot says they want timeboxed review; no customer notification yet. we should still assume possible partial exposure of API keys. issuing immediate recommend: rotate any staging API keys with 48h lookback and alert if anomalous issuance from listed IPs.
eli-sre: quick checklist done: blocked public-read ACL, revoked service keys, snapshot stored, identified objects. holding deletion.
maya-oncall: handing off to night oncall @noah-oncall in 30m. will summarize current state: ACL fixed, keys rotated, snapshots saved, deletion pending legal sign-off, prod unaffected. If anything new or customer impact arises, page me. :thumbsup:
noah-oncall: on-call takeover acknowledged. will monitor logs and blocklisted IPs at infra layer. if legal clears, will execute deletion ticket and confirm.
legal-bot: acknowledged. created case INC-1819012345 for records; legal review ETA 2 hours. request: preserve timestamps and copies in secure-case-bucket.
maya-oncall: thanks team. closing immediate pager but leaving thread open for handoff notes. :heart:
incident-bot: INCIDENT UPDATED: status -> containment in progress. owners: maya-oncall, noah-oncall, lisa-security. link: https://incidents.redwood/1819012345
